value.body: Going to college after Class 12 means choosing an undergraduate degree — B.A., B.Sc., B.Com., B.Tech, MBBS, LLB and many more — usually lasting 3 to 5 years. The degree shapes which jobs, entrance exams and postgraduate options open up later, although many careers stay reachable from more than one degree.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 3 years for most B.A./B.Sc./B.Com.; 4 for B.Tech; 5 for B.Arch and integrated LLB; MBBS adds an internship

items.label: Gross Enrolment Ratio (18–23 yrs)
items.note: Share of the 18–23 age group in higher education

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Suits students who want a recognised degree before working, or whose target career requires one — medicine, law, engineering, architecture, teaching, and most government officer posts. Admission is through Class 12 marks, CUET-UG (central and many other universities), or course-specific tests such as NEET-UG, JEE Main, NATA, CLAT and state CETs.

value.title: At a glance
items: It means 3–5 years of fees and living costs before a full-time salary; government colleges and scholarships lower the cost.
A graduate degree is the minimum requirement for many government exams, including UPSC Civil Services, SSC CGL and bank PO/clerk exams.
Outcomes depend heavily on the institution and on the skills built alongside the degree, not only on the degree name.
Distance and open-university degrees let some students study while working.

value.note: All levels (PhD to certificate), including estimation for non-responding institutions.
